name: Akamai WAF SIEM
summary: Newline-delimited WAF events plus an offset trailer, which is what the XSOAR Akamai WAF SIEM integration parses.
notes: Set the integration Server URL to the catch URL shown in PAN Parrot. XSOAR joins that host with /siem/v1/configs/{configIds}.

Each response is one JSON object per line. The last line is { total, offset, limit }, matching the pack's test fixture. There is no trailing blank line, so the current get_events_with_offset parser can pop the trailer.
Non-empty rule* fields are URL-encoded base64, which decode_message() expects. The pack's unit-test fixture leaves those fields empty; both are accepted.
httpMessage.start is a unix-seconds string. The integration does int(start) and datetime.utcfromtimestamp.

Checked against https://techdocs.akamai.com/siem-integration/reference/get-config on 2026-11-09. Official limit default is 10000 and the maximum is 600000. This mock returns at most 500 events and 2 MB, then an offset.
If from and offset are both set, Akamai uses the time window. This mock ignores offset when from is present.
httpMessage.query is required by the public event schema. botData, clientData, and userRiskData are omitted.
Production offset tokens are long. This mock uses a shorter pp_ token. 416 for an expired offset is not simulated.
attribution: Field names and encoding follow Packs/Akamai_SIEM in https://github.com/demisto/content (MIT). See /presets/ATTRIBUTION.md.

source.name: Akamai WAF SIEM
source.attribution: Checked against Akamai's SIEM integration reference and demisto/content (MIT).

differences: Akamai's default limit is 10000 and the documented maximum is 600000. This mock returns at most 500 events and 2 MB per call, then an offset.
If from and offset are both present, Akamai uses time mode. This mock does the same.
Production offset tokens are long opaque strings. This mock uses a shorter pp_ token that still round-trips.
botData, clientData, and userRiskData are omitted. httpMessage.query is included because the public event schema requires it.
Akamai 429 bodies are application/problem+json. Chaos errors here are a small JSON object, with Retry-After on 429 and 503.

notes: Server URL should be this endpoint's catch URL. The integration requests /siem/v1/configs/{configIds}.

operations.summary: Security events for one or more config IDs (semicolon-separated).
